open_questions.q: How many of the SMBGCs called in the 87-genome corpus are genuinely novel (no MIBiG hit at BiG-SCAPE distance <0.30) versus already-known BGCs, and does the marine-Streptomyces new-vs-known ratio actually exceed that of a matched terrestrial-Streptomyces set of equal genome-count and size distribution?
open_questions.basis: Xu et al. relied on antiSMASH KnownClusterBlast/SubClusterBlast for BGC identity assignments but did not report a formal MIBiG-referenced novelty score at a BiG-SCAPE distance threshold, and this replication pass did not run antiSMASH at all. The paper's implicit argument that marine Streptomyces are a rich source of novel chemistry rests on cluster counts, not on validated novelty against MIBiG.
next_steps: Run antiSMASH v6 on the 141 QC-passing marine set and a size-matched 141-genome terrestrial-Streptomyces control set drawn from BV-BRC.
Feed the GBK outputs into BiG-SCAPE with MIBiG 3.1 as reference; count clusters with no MIBiG neighbor at cutoff 0.30.
Report new-vs-known ratio per corpus with bootstrap CI; test the marine/terrestrial difference with a permutation test rather than Kruskal-Wallis to avoid the paper's parametric assumptions.

open_questions.q: Is the BGC-class distribution of marine Streptomyces (per-genome fractions of PKS-I, PKS-II, NRPS, hybrid, terpene, RiPP, other) statistically distinguishable from a matched terrestrial-Streptomyces set once genome size, ANI-based redundancy, and assembly-quality tier are controlled for?
open_questions.basis: The paper documents BGC class ranges for the marine set but never runs a matched-control comparison against terrestrial Streptomyces. Any 'marine strains are enriched in class X' framing is therefore descriptive, not comparative. This replication pass confirmed universal class presence in the marine set (PKS/NRPS/terpene in 11-12 of 12) but likewise did not benchmark against a terrestrial control.
next_steps: Assemble a terrestrial-Streptomyces control matched 1:1 on genome-size decile and CheckM tier from BV-BRC (~141 genomes).
Run identical antiSMASH v6 pipeline; compute per-genome class fraction vectors.
Test marine-vs-terrestrial with PERMANOVA on the class-composition Bray-Curtis matrix; report effect size R^2 and permutation p, not just significance.

open_questions.q: How sensitive are the paper's per-genome BGC counts and per-class ranges (16-84 SMBGCs, 2-38 PKs, 1-15 NRPS, 2-6 terpene) to antiSMASH version and strictness setting -- specifically, do the same 87 genomes yield materially different counts under antiSMASH v5-relaxed (paper), v6-relaxed, v6-strict, and v7-relaxed?
open_questions.basis: antiSMASH cluster-boundary algorithms have changed non-trivially between v4, v5, v6, and v7 (added detection rules, revised RiPP handling, changed hybrid-cluster logic). Xu et al. used a specific 2018-era version. Downstream ecological claims (density, class composition, clade correlation) are only as stable as the underlying cluster-count reproducibility.
next_steps: Rebuild the paper's exact 87-strain accession list (blocked by MDPI 403; workaround: request from corresponding author).
Run antiSMASH v5.1-relaxed (as close to paper's version as possible), v6.1-relaxed, v6.1-strict, v7.0-relaxed on all 87 genomes with identical extras.
Report per-genome count matrix (87 x 4 versions) and per-class range under each; compute Kendall tau of per-genome-rank BGC counts across versions.
State explicitly which of the paper's numeric ranges survive under which version.

open_questions.q: Does host niche (sponge/coral-associated vs sediment-derived vs seawater-planktonic) predict BGC-count, BGC-class composition, or BGC novelty beyond what is already predicted by phylogenetic placement (Clade I/II/III), and are the paper's 'Clade I+sediment more specific / Clade II+invertebrate more total' claims robust to ecotype-metadata cleanup?
open_questions.basis: Xu et al.'s headline biological claim is a phylotype x ecotype interaction, but isolation_source metadata in GenBank is notoriously noisy (strings like 'marine sediment', 'deep-sea sediment', 'sponge Haliclona', 'sponge, unspecified' are inconsistently curated). The paper accepted GenBank ecotype strings without a documented cleanup. This replication pass observed sediment=84, sponge=25 dominance today, but did not test the interaction claim at all.
next_steps: Curate isolation_source strings for the 87 (and the 141 superset) into a controlled vocabulary (sediment/sponge/coral/tunicate/mollusk/algae/seawater/cyanobacterium/mangrove/unknown).
After building the phylogenomic tree (OQ3 side-effect), fit a mixed model: BGC_count ~ ecotype * clade + genome_size + (1|host-family).
Report main effects, interaction, marginal R^2, and whether the interaction survives phylogenetic-independence correction (PGLS).

open_questions.q: For the marine-Streptomyces BGCs called by antiSMASH but absent from MIBiG (the putative 'novel' set from OQ1), what fraction have been chemically/functionally validated in wet lab -- i.e., what is the wet-lab hit-rate when a marine-Streptomyces novel-BGC prediction is followed to heterologous expression or isolate-culture activity assay?
open_questions.basis: The entire practical rationale for surveying marine-Streptomyces BGCs is drug-discovery leads, but the paper (like the field generally) never closes the loop from bioinformatic prediction to validated activity. Without a hit-rate estimate, the BGC-count claims are structural, not translational.
next_steps: Cross-reference the novel-BGC set (from OQ1) against Natural Products Atlas, LOTUS, and StreptomeDB for any reported isolated compound from the same strain-BGC pair.
PubMed/Europe PMC-mine the 87 strain names for wet-lab activity reports (heterologous expression, culture-broth bioassay, LC-MS/MS mining) published 2019-2026.

Report the empirical prediction-to-validation hit-rate with strain-level provenance and note whether marine-Streptomyces predictions validate at a materially different rate than the ~3-5% baseline reported for terrestrial actinomycetes.
